notes: Centralizes unquoted-brace detection in Token/Dispenser helpers and applies it consistently across the dispenser, parser, import, and blockTokens paths, which fixes the root cause rather than one call site; it is backed by thorough dispenser, parser, and adapt integration tests, with only minor untouched edge cases such as import-arg substitution.

The patch fixes the root cause by adding `isOpenCurlyBrace`/`isCloseCurlyBrace` helpers on `Token` and `Dispenser` that check `wasQuoted`, and uses them at every brace check in the dispenser and parser (`NextArg`, `NextBlock`, `addresses`, `directives`, `doImport`, `directive`, `blockTokens`, `openCurlyBrace`/`closeCurlyBrace`); it removes the now-redundant `wasQuoted` check in `directive()` and adds focused dispenser, parser and adapt tests covering double-quoted and backtick braces, nesting and the unclosed-block error.

This fixes the main bug: every same-module import block for a for_each/count resource is now kept, in a stable order. But a parent block still overrides child blocks at the whole-resource level, so a parent import of one instance silently drops child imports of other instances (the same silent-drop pattern the issue reports). Changing the return type to a bare slice is a reasonable design choice but may break the expected API, and only 1/3 hidden tests pass. The added unit and plan-level tests are thorough, covering reversed order, count, child module and root-into-child.

Returning a slice instead of a map keyed by ConfigResource fixes the reported case where several import blocks target instances of one resource in the same module. However, parent-over-child override still works per whole resource, so a child's import of a different instance is silently dropped whenever the parent imports any instance of that resource; that is the same silent-drop failure the issue reports, and it likely explains the 1/3 hidden-test result.

The transform hooks in after config consolidation and before shortcut derivation, so it covers run, cloud run, local execution and archive in one place. It keeps exec, env, tags and browser options, rejects multiple scenarios and conflicting shortcut flags with InvalidConfig, and is backed by thorough unit and end-to-end tests; the main gap is that shortcuts set through env vars are silently discarded rather than rejected.

Applies `--once` right after config consolidation and before scenario derivation. It keeps the single scenario's exec, env, tags and options, swaps the executor to shared-iterations with 1 VU and 1 iteration, rejects multiple scenarios and conflicting shortcut flags with clear errors, and is tested at unit, run, archive and cloud levels; the only minor gap is that env-var shortcuts such as K6_VUS are silently discarded rather than rejected.

Adds an optional `Dir` override, used only when a section, taxonomy or term ancestor has a slug, and builds it by walking up parent sections; it respects disablePathToLower, keeps `url` and permalink precedence, leaves existing URLs unchanged, and the test covers bundles, non-section subdirectories, nested sections, taxonomies and terms, though `:sections` permalink tokens still ignore section slugs and the parent walk is not memoized.

Adds a `Dir` override to TargetPathDescriptor and computes it by walking up the section ancestors and applying slugs, which correctly relocates sections, taxonomies, terms, nested sections, leaf bundles, and pages in plain subdirectories; it respects DisablePathToLower, though slugs are ignored when permalinks config is present and the ancestor walk is recomputed for every page.

Fixes the root cause by wrapping a parenthesised *NumberLiteral in a unary-ADD *DurationExpr with Wrapped=true, and correctly extends the parse-time zero/non-positive checks (positive duration, division, modulo) to see through the new wrapper so existing errors are preserved. Tests are thorough, covering parser AST, printer round-trips and promqltest evaluation; minor nits are that the wrapper's position range excludes the parens and that the AST shape changes for `+(5)` and `-(5)`.

Fixes the round-trip loss by wrapping a parenthesised NumberLiteral in a Wrapped unary-ADD DurationExpr, and the new durationLiteralValue helper keeps the parse-time checks (non-positive range, division/modulo by zero) working through the new wrapper; the synthetic node is slightly indirect and its StartPos ignores the paren, but the change is focused and well tested across printer, parser and promqltest eval cases.

This implements the sentinel `ReturnError` approach the issue asks for: `return` panics out of `evalCall`, is trapped in `executeWithState` and `walkTemplate`, and the fork script is updated to match. It also removes the old return-wrapper transform, adds a small `wrapReturnArgs` rewrite for backward compatibility, and includes thorough integration tests. However, it changes `{{ return }}` semantics (it now yields the output rendered so far), edits an existing test's expected error to fit the new behavior, can leave partial-decorator push/pop calls unbalanced on early return, and one hidden test plus the package suite still fail.

This is a well-built sentinel-error design: a panic/recover ReturnError is trapped in executeWithState and walkTemplate, `try` re-panics it, the fork script is updated, and the old transform/wrapper complexity is removed. However, the custom wrapReturnArgs rewrite changes `return x | f` pipeline semantics, which forced the candidate to rewrite an existing test's expected error. That rewrite likely explains the failing hidden test and package suite, and edits to existing test expectations are a red flag.
